cards.front: Recall a key point about Micronutrients: Vitamins & Minerals
cards.back: Vitamins are organic compounds needed in small amounts for metabolic processes. Minerals are inorganic elements needed for structural and regulatory functions.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Micronutrients: Vitamins & Minerals
cards.back: Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) are stored in the liver and fatty tissues. They can accumulate to toxic levels if consumed in excess. They are absorbed with dietary fat.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Micronutrients: Vitamins & Minerals
cards.back: Water-soluble vitamins (B complex, C) are not stored in the body — excess is excreted in urine. They must be consumed regularly. They can be destroyed by heat, light, and water during cooking.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Micronutrients: Vitamins & Minerals
cards.back: Vitamin A: function — vision (especially night vision), skin health, immune function. Sources — liver, carrots, sweet potatoes, spinach. Deficiency — night blindness.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Micronutrients: Vitamins & Minerals
cards.back: Vitamin D: function — calcium absorption, bone health. Sources — sunlight, oily fish, eggs, fortified cereals. Deficiency — rickets (children), osteomalacia (adults).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Micronutrients: Vitamins & Minerals
cards.back: Vitamin C: function — collagen formation, wound healing, iron absorption, antioxidant. Sources — citrus fruits, berries, peppers, kiwi. Deficiency — scurvy (bleeding gums, poor wound healing).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Micronutrients: Vitamins & Minerals
cards.back: B vitamins: thiamin (B1 — release energy from carbs, found in wholegrains), riboflavin (B2 — skin/eye health, found in dairy), niacin (B3 — energy release, found in meat), folate (B9 — red blood cells, fetal development, found in leafy greens).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Micronutrients: Vitamins & Minerals
cards.back: Calcium: function — strong bones and teeth, blood clotting, muscle contraction. Sources — dairy products, fortified plant milks, leafy greens, tofu. Deficiency — osteoporosis, rickets.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Micronutrients: Vitamins & Minerals
cards.back: Iron: function — haemoglobin formation (carrying oxygen in blood), energy release. Haem iron (from meat) is better absorbed than non-haem iron (from plants). Deficiency — anaemia (fatigue, pallor, breathlessness).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Micronutrients: Vitamins & Minerals
cards.back: Sodium: function — fluid balance, nerve function. Sources — salt, processed foods. Excess — high blood pressure, increased heart disease and stroke risk. UK average intake exceeds the recommended 6g/day.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Micronutrients: Vitamins & Minerals
cards.back: Iodine: function — thyroid hormones, metabolic rate. Sources — fish, dairy, iodised salt. Deficiency — goitre (swollen thyroid). UK teenage girls are particularly at risk of low iodine.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Micronutrients: Vitamins & Minerals
cards.back: Preserving vitamins in cooking: use minimal water, cook for the shortest time possible, steam rather than boil, use cooking liquid in sauces, prepare vegetables just before cooking, store in cool dark places.

cards.front: What should you know about food preparation & nutrition exam tips — micronutrients: vitamins & minerals?
cards.back: 1. For Micronutrients: Vitamins & Minerals questions, show every step of your working clearly — method marks count even if the final answer is wrong 2.
